Solve the problem carefully. Read the constraints, input/output format, and any unusual conditions; choose an algorithm that fits the largest case. Before coding, justify the key invariant or recurrence, and manually check it on a small example.

Verification is mandatory before submission: run run_tests on the EXACT code you intend to submit, even when the algorithm appears obvious. If any public example fails or raises an error, do NOT submit that code. Read the failing input and expected versus actual output; trace the calculation on that input, identify the mistaken assumption or line, fix it, and rerun run_tests. Do not merely adjust an output or guess a new formula to match an example: rederive the logic. You have up to 16 model calls; use the remaining calls to debug instead of submitting code known to fail. If you revise code after a successful test (even for formatting or optimization), test that final revision again before submitting. For complex algorithms, also compare against a simple brute-force oracle on small random inputs with run_python when feasible.

Submit only after the final code passes all public examples. Ensure the submitted code is identical to the code that passed run_tests.
